page: Microsoft Azure E80is_v4 is an isolated, memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The system is driven by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor based on the x86_64 architecture, operating at a base frequency of 2.6 GHz. It provides 80 dedicated virtual CPUs backed by 40 physical cores with symmetric multithreading, alongside 504.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 6.3 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware vector instruction sets including AVX-512 and AVX-512 VNNI are supported. The instance features no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistence, and includes zero onboard GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel compute and memory subsystem performance. The instance achieves a PassMark CPU score of 53,311.42 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 74,314.11, placing both metrics in the upper quartile. High-bandwidth memory tests reflect uncached large-block read speeds of 212.31 GB/sec and write throughput of 96.19 GB/sec, driving superior results in data-intensive tests such as PassMark database operations (22,753.51) and Redis SET throughput reaching 64.02 million operations per second. Multi-threaded compilation and decompression benchmarks similarly achieve high performance percentiles.

In contrast, single-threaded metrics remain within the median range due to the conservative 2.6 GHz clock profile, evidenced by Geekbench single-core scores of 1,357.0 and stress-ng single-core output of 1,483.18. In addition, the lack of dedicated GPU hardware produces low generative tokens-per-second scores in LLM text generation tasks. Cost efficiency is driven by high memory density and full hardware isolation on a single node rather than low single-thread costs. The instance is well suited for large in-memory databases, Redis cache grids, large-scale software build systems, and enterprise data processing pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure E80is_v4 is a dedicated, memory-optimized instance providing 80 vCPUs and 40 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor at 2.6 GHz. Operating on the x86_64 architecture with Hyper-V virtualization, it offers 504.0 GB of RAM with full hardware isolation. It contains no bundled local storage and zero GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage options. Benchmark testing shows upper-quartile parallel compute and memory throughput, highlighted by 64.02 million Redis operations per second, a PassMark database score of 22,753.51, and large-block uncached memory read bandwidth of 212.31 GB/sec. Single-core processing metrics and LLM generation remain moderate to low due to modest clock rates and absence of hardware accelerators. The instance delivers high resource density for in-memory databases, analytics caches, and concurrent enterprise workloads.
